fw-update/device_updater.cpp.message:
I am against adding logs like these in pldm code base. If we need more readable logs, please feel free to add fw_update spec support to pldm dissector in Wireshark.

IBM took a lot of effort in getting the base & platform spec supported in pldm wireshark dissecter. Dont want the code base to be polluted with these logs in yet another verbose option.

The bulk of PLDM T5 traffic is the Tx/Rx of RequestFirmwareData where PLDM FD downloads image from the BMC. With the number of PLDM devices we support on a platform, the total amount of data we transfer exceeds 140+ M, capturing MCTP traffic for this and adding it to BMC dump is not a feasible solution. 

So printing Tx/Rx for the RequestFirmwareData without the actual data firmware data, gives decent debug capabilities on the BMC when PLDM firmware update is in progress and helped us triage issues where logs on the device has been insufficient.

I agree with Manoj's concern in principle, there are platform specific needs where such flexibility is needed. Also unlike a feature flag where more forethought is needed, flag for debug tracing has minimal side effects.

From what I could see online Wireshark helps analyze the network traffic, but in the case of FW Update using large bundles (>140M) the packets captured would make it hard to debug any FW Update failures for specific components. These logs would help speed up the debug process

> capturing MCTP traffic for this and adding it to BMC dump is not a feasible solution.

If this needs to be captured as part of the BMC dump, can we not just add them as `INFO` messages written into the journal, rather than a new verbose option which under the cover puts things into the journal ? I also disagree with adding such logs. I agree that a pcap/Wireshark is a much more concise approach. You don't have to capture all traffic on an interface, you can be selective. See e.g. [tcpdump](https://www.tcpdump.org/manpages/tcpdump.1.html)'s filter expressions and [pcap-filter](https://www.tcpdump.org/manpages/pcap-filter.7.html). /COMMIT_MSG.message:
@andrew@codeconstruct.com.au - can you add below to the commit message, it would be beneficial to add some additional details in case if some one accidentally looks at this commit with not much of background on the problem.

The original design of the Requester D-Bus API lacked ergonomic considerations. While it offered allocation functionality, it did not provide a corresponding mechanism to release instance IDs. Additionally, the interface failed to address critical issues, such as handling instance ID cleanup in the event of application crashes, and allowed applications to specify timeouts that exceeded the limits defined by the PLDM specification. Consequently, pldmd was forced to monitor all PLDM traffic and implement workarounds to manage instance ID lifecycles on behalf of applications, effectively assuming the role of global instance ID manager.

Additionally, many applications duplicated PLDM logic—implementing their own retry mechanisms—and, in some cases, violated the PLDM specification by setting timeouts as high as 40 seconds.

Now that all applications rely directly on the libpldm allocator, it makes sense to remove this legacy interface entirely to prevent any future usage.
